subject: Special Education Compliance and Ad Hoc Reports
overview: The Committee received a positive state audit of its special education programs and approved amended requests for data on school fossil fuel usage and pandemic-related IEP identification. Members also addressed public concerns regarding a subcommittee proposal to discourage speakers from stating their length of residency during meetings.

items.title: Executive Session
items.summary: The committee entered executive session to discuss strategy for collective bargaining and ongoing litigation in the case of Amico versus City of Medford.

items.title: Routine Approvals and Minutes
items.summary: Approved various sets of minutes, bills, transfer of funds, and payrolls while tabling reports on the harassment policy and special education budget hearings.

items.title: Public Participation and Residency Statement Controversy
items.summary: Residents addressed dyslexia services and criticized a subcommittee proposal to discourage speakers from mentioning their length of residency, a policy members agreed to revisit.

items.title: Superintendent's Update
items.summary: Dr. Edouard-Vincent memorialized educator Dennis Moriarty, recognized student mathematics awards, and provided updates on senior class graduation events.

items.title: COVID-19 Health and Policy Update
items.summary: Health officials reported low positivity rates in schools and announced expanded vaccine eligibility for students 12 and older, while confirming that mask mandates will remain in place through the end of the school year.

items.title: Special Education Tiered Focused Monitoring Report
items.summary: Director Joan Bowen presented a state report showing full compliance with special education regulations and a commendable rating for the district's collaboration with the Parent Advisory Council.

items.title: Administrative Recommendations
items.summary: Accepted a $300 donation for the Fine Arts department, maintained current MEEP tuition rates, and voted to reject the state's school choice program for the upcoming year.

items.title: Elementary School Presentations
items.summary: Principals from McGlynn and Roberts elementary schools highlighted student resilience, academic progress, and community enrichment activities during the transition to in-person learning.

items.title: Fossil Fuel Utilization Report Request
items.summary: Approved an amended request for the administration to determine a feasibility timeline for a report on converting school buildings to all-electric systems.

items.title: IEP Identification Report Request
items.summary: Approved a request for the administration to provide comparative data on student IEP identification rates to assess the pandemic's impact on service referrals.

items.title: Condolences and Adjournment
items.summary: The committee recognized the passing of several community members and school staff with a moment of silence before adjourning.
